thesis_at_purchase_vs_now: Consolidation and disciplined capacity: broken; the industry now faces a complete collapse in demand due to pandemic restrictions and travel bans [D01], [D06].
Durable competitive advantage: broken; the future economics are unknowable as demand for travel is no longer identical to the existence of the franchise [D01].
Pricing power: broken; high fixed costs and perishable capacity lead to non-linear cash losses as traffic falls, and public assistance may result in dilution for existing owners [D05], [D06].
final.price_vs_value_now: The market prices reflect a state of distress with high uncertainty regarding normalized earnings; pre-pandemic P/E multiples of 2.7x to 8.3x are no longer reliable indicators of value [D04].
final.after_tax_hurdle: Tax cost is secondary; the primary concern is avoiding permanent loss of capital as the airline industry's business model faces a structural interruption [D05].

drivers.driver: The economic thesis of a disciplined, profitable airline industry has been invalidated by an unforeseeable, systemic demand shock [D01].
The business environment is now unknowable, and the duration of depressed demand makes future cash generation and survival highly speculative [D01], [D06].
Airlines carry heavy fixed costs and debt burdens, which, in the absence of travel demand, threaten to cause permanent impairment of shareholder equity [D05], [D06].
Public assistance under the CARES Act, while providing liquidity, may impose restrictions or dilution that fundamentally alter the rights of existing common owners [D03], [D05].

final.memo:
When the facts change, I must change my mind. My original thesis for the airlines centered on the industry finally achieving rational capacity discipline and sustained profitability [D01], [D07]. Today, the world has changed in a way that makes the future of the travel industry essentially unknowable [D01]. 

We are facing a situation where demand has evaporated, and because airlines operate with high fixed costs and perishable capacity, the cash losses are non-linear and severe [D01], [D05]. While the CARES Act provides a potential lifeline, this support often comes at the cost of dilution or restrictive conditions for the common shareholder [D03], [D05]. I do not know how long the demand will remain depressed or what the industry will look like on the other side of this crisis [D06].

I do not anchor on cost, and I will not wait for a recovery that is no longer within my circle of competence to predict [D07]. We must avoid the permanent loss of capital, and when the underlying economic advantage of a business is fundamentally compromised, the only prudent course is to exit [D05].
uncited_claims: Buffett's personal decision-making process for exiting the airline positions as of April 2, 2020.
